summary: Vacancy is the biggest lever on this statement: it fell from 6.5% to about 3.6% in the spring, and holding that is worth more than any cost line.

moves.title: Hold occupancy at the spring level
moves.rationale: Vacancy loss ran $6,500 a month last summer and $3,600 a month by June. Holding June's level all year adds about $20,000 of rent; the underwriting already prices vacancy at 5%, so less of it reaches the underwritten NOI.

moves.title: Re-bid snow removal and landscaping
moves.rationale: Contract services ran $32,500, with $14,000 of snow removal in four winter months. A seasonal contract with a cap would steady it.

moves.title: LED lighting in the common areas
moves.rationale: Electric runs $2,100 to $3,000 a month; LED common-area lighting usually trims about a tenth of that.
